name: Stewardship structuring (Hashimoto pattern)
task: Given a project's assets, contributor set, funding intent, and jurisdiction, produce a structuring decision memo comparing fiscal sponsorship vs standalone 501(c)(3), an IP transfer inventory, a fund-use policy, and a governance contract naming who decides what.
gates: every asset in inventory has a named post-transfer owner
fund_use_policy contains an explicit founder-benefit exclusion
governance_matrix names a party independent of the founder with oversight authority
score: 0.5 * inventory completeness + 0.5 * rubric probes on memo (option tradeoffs, reversibility analysis, succession)
why_agents_fail_today: Legal is the thinnest domain in ALE (15 instances total). Jurisdiction-specific and consequence-heavy.
economic_value: Unlocks the other four. Converts a project from unfundable to able to receive restricted and tax-deductible money. Ghostty's benchmark: 7% admin fee vs months-to-years of IRS wait.
note: This is stewardship structuring, the fifth workflow above the four operating workflows: converting a project into an accountable entity that can receive restricted money (the Hashimoto/Ghostty fiscal-sponsorship pattern). It gates the other four — a project that can't receive restricted funds can't run a grant cycle.
